Erin (Security): Heads up — running a quick design/Q for backups+snapshots encryption across DBs and object store. We need to lock down the flow for cross-account restores and ensure RBAC + audit logging captures key usage. Anyone free to weigh in?
Samir (SRE): I'm in. main concerns: who can grant decrypt on a restore, and how we avoid accidental exposure when rotating keys. :eyes:
Jia (Eng-ML): Also: model artifacts live in the same buckets as some staging data. If we change KMS keys we must not break historical eval replays. Need a plan for key aliases.
Mike (Infra): The ask I heard: 1) enforce SSE-KMS for S3 buckets holding snapshots, 2) make DB snapshots use CMKs, 3) define an RBAC path for restore ops that is auditable. Is that right?
Erin (Security): Yep. Bonus: we should consider ephemeral grants for runbook restores (time-limited decrypt grants) instead of broad IAM roles. That reduces blast radius.
Samir (SRE): Ephemeral grants via STS session + KMS Grant looks good. But we need a clear on-call playbook when a key is compromised. I can draft a flow: revoke grants -> rotate key -> re-encrypt critical backups -> update alias. Thoughts?
Mike (Infra): Draft IAM/KMS policy I tested in staging — allows decrypt only if request has `aws:TagKeys` from our restore workflow. Example snippet: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/restore-runbook"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:CreateGrant","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:restore-id": "${aws:RequestTag/restore-id}"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
Mike (Infra): This forces the restore tool to tag the request and makes audit logs easier to parse.
Jia (Eng-ML): Will the ML training infra be able to replay older experiments if the key is rotated? We need to keep old keys for at least N months or provide rewrap tooling.
Erin (Security): Good call. Let's set a retention policy: keep previous CMKs for 90 days with automated re-encrypt job for any snapshot newer than that. For legal holds we can extend.
Samir (SRE): On logging — we must capture KMS:CreateGrant and KMS:RevokeGrant in CloudTrail and forward to log-archive with alerts when grants are created by non-service principals. I can add a Sigma rule.
Erin (Security): Also surface bucket-level SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS difference: for tenant-level secrets we must use KMS. For generic static assets SSE-S3 okay but prefer SSE-KMS because we need auditability.
KMS Bot: Note: cross-account decrypt requires either key policy allowing the other account principal or a grant created in the key account. Creating a grant is simpler but must be audited.
oncall-bot: Incident workflow reminder — for suspected key compromise, follow runbook ID #enc-restore-2024 — page 4 has revoke+rotate steps.
Samir (SRE): Vulnerability triage note: we found snapshot metadata with tenant_id in object metadata visible to listing users via a staging IAM bug. Impact: info leak only, but could map tenants to snapshots. We've scoped affected snapshots (bucket: redwood-snap-prod, prefix: snapshots/staging/).
Erin (Security): Triage: Mark as P2, rotate any keys that may have been used for those buckets, scrub metadata (re-write objects without tenant_id), and notify legal if customer data map could be reconstructed. Samir, can you run a scrub job and create a ticket?
Samir (SRE): On it. I'll run a scrub and produce a small report. ETA 2 hours. I'll also add an automated check in the snapshot pipeline to reject objects with tenant metadata unless explicitly flagged.
Mike (Infra): For cross-account restores (partner ops), prefer creating short-lived grants instead of updating key policy. We can automate grant creation via our restore service: it calls `CreateGrant` with `Constraints` and a TTL. Remember to call `RetireGrant` after completion.
Jia (Eng-ML): For model artifact replayability: schedule rewrap job that re-encrypts older artifacts under current key alias and stores provenance in metadata (but not PII). That way experiments can still run.
Erin (Security): Action items: Samir — scrub + add pipeline guard + draft Sigma alert for grant creation by non-service principals. Mike — prototype ephemeral grant flow and sample policy snippet into infra repo. Jia — define replay/rewrap requirements and retention window. I'll update the runbook with these steps and add the 90-day key overlap policy.
Samir (SRE): Confirmed. I'll post the scrub result in this thread and open a ticket in Security board.
Mike (Infra): I'll open a PR with the KMS helper lambda and example `CreateGrant` usage. Tagging @Erin for review.
Erin (Security): Thanks all — this feels actionable. If anything blocks restore tooling, ping me. :thumbsup:
